Quick triage notes (on-call):
- Observed spike in 5xx and 429s starting 07:49 ET from the same client IP subnets tied to Paramount.
- Auth validation service (auth-validate-v2) is returning a transient internal error when it receives tokens with "nbf"/"iat" slightly in the future due to clock skew; that internal error path surfaces as 500 within the gateway under high concurrency.
- Under retry storms, the validation service is saturating its worker pool and falling through to a generic 429 response path that the gateway relays to the client. So both 500 and 429 are seen but root cause is token validation + retry amplification.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:40 ET):
1) Added a 30s clock-skew grace in the validation layer for JWT "nbf/iat" checks to accept slightly-future tokens for known Paramount client IDs.
2) Enabled a temporary 401/403 mapping for auth failures instead of surfacing 5xx when validation explicitly fails — this will help clients stop retrying.
3) Put client-rate limits (soft) on the problematic IP subnets to slow retry storms.
4) Increased worker pool for auth-validate-v2 by +30% temporarily.

Next: gather full logs, reproduce with sample token, push a PR to fix the error-path mapping (INF-7719). Tessa, if you can drive the controlled rollout notes and notify Paramount ops.

- Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
